html:
Aussa is an oasis on the lower Awash River in the Afar lowlands of what is now north-eastern Ethiopia. The map shows a state there from 1650 to 1800. Its history has two phases.

In 1577 the leader of the Adal Sultanate moved his seat from Harar to Aussa, away from Oromo attacks. This Imamate of Aussa was a weak heir of the Adal state that had once fought Ethiopia under Imam Ahmad. It fell apart in the 1670s, overrun by the local Afar.

In the 1730s an Afar dynasty, the Mudaito, founded the Sultanate of Aussa. It became the leading Afar state, controlling caravan routes and salt between the Ethiopian highlands and the Red Sea coast. It kept much self-rule after Menelik II brought it under Ethiopia in the late 1800s.
